title_vi: CDN phổ biến vì đâu, và máy chủ biên lưu những gì

related.reason_vi: Bài CDN cho người mới đặt máy chủ biên cạnh điện toán biên và chơi game trên mây.
CDN là một trong các tầng bộ nhớ đệm từ trình duyệt tới cơ sở dữ liệu.
Một bài khác của nguồn cũng giải thích CDN.

claims.claim_vi: A shared cache stores responses for reuse by more than one user, usually as part of an intermediary; a private cache is dedicated to a single user, often in a user agent.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of httpwg/httpwg.github.io at commit 03f35d852e7b64668ab08fda1a8076d6d44d17ae, the head of its default branch when read on 2026-10-18 (a later change to that branch does not alter this URL).

claims.claim_vi: The unqualified private response directive means a shared cache MUST NOT store the response; no-store applies to private and shared caches; s-maxage overrides max-age and Expires for a shared cache.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of httpwg/httpwg.github.io at commit 03f35d852e7b64668ab08fda1a8076d6d44d17ae, the head of its default branch when read on 2026-10-18 (a later change to that branch does not alter this URL).

claims.claim_vi: Caching is an entirely OPTIONAL feature of HTTP; the cache requirements focus on preventing a cache from storing or reusing responses inappropriately, so storing a public response is permitted, not required.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of httpwg/httpwg.github.io at commit 03f35d852e7b64668ab08fda1a8076d6d44d17ae, the head of its default branch when read on 2026-10-18 (a later change to that branch does not alter this URL).

claims.claim_vi: The Set-Cookie response header field does not inhibit caching; servers that wish to control caching of such responses are encouraged to emit appropriate Cache-Control header fields.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of httpwg/httpwg.github.io at commit 03f35d852e7b64668ab08fda1a8076d6d44d17ae, the head of its default branch when read on 2026-10-18 (a later change to that branch does not alter this URL).

claims.claim_vi: A cache MAY assign a heuristic expiration time when no explicit one is given; it is not required to.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of httpwg/httpwg.github.io at commit 03f35d852e7b64668ab08fda1a8076d6d44d17ae, the head of its default branch when read on 2026-10-18 (a later change to that branch does not alter this URL).

claims.claim_vi: With nginx 1.24.0 proxy_cache and no other cache settings, each path requested three times: public, max-age=60 gave MISS, HIT, HIT (origin hit once); max-age=60, s-maxage=2 gave MISS, HIT, HIT and EXPIRED after 3 s (origin hit twice); private, no-store, a public response with Set-Cookie, and a response with no Cache-Control were never stored (origin hit three times each).
claims.verified_by: Experiment run by the author on 2026-10-18 on one virtual machine: Python http.server origin on 127.0.0.1 and nginx 1.24.0 (Ubuntu package) with proxy_cache_path and add_header X-Cache-Status $upstream_cache_status; requests sent with curl, origin request counts read from the origin.

claims.claim_vi: MDN lists CDN benefits (less load on own servers, servers nearer users, preconfigured caching) and downsides: a third-party dependency that can fail or be blocked, an extra attack vector, and possibly worse performance because of extra DNS lookups and connections and no cross-origin cache sharing in modern browsers.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of mdn/content at commit a1aa79c09717761fc72c20bac94bb9c430ed487a, the head of its default branch when read on 2026-10-18 (a later change to that branch does not alter this URL).

claims.claim_vi: With a managed cache such as a CDN, stored responses can be deleted at any time through dashboards or API calls, which the HTTP caching specification itself does not define.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of mdn/content at commit a1aa79c09717761fc72c20bac94bb9c430ed487a, the head of its default branch when read on 2026-10-18 (a later change to that branch does not alter this URL).

claims.claim_vi: CDN request flow (edge checks its cache, forwards to origin on a miss, stores a copy), components (origin, edge servers, DNS, control plane) and request routing (GSLB, anycast DNS, IXPs).
